learning_outcomes.text: Ability to identify claims, evidence, and assumptions in argumentative texts.
Ability to analyze how arguments are structured and how evidence supports claims.
Formulate clear and concise thesis statements in response to argumentative writing tasks.
Ability to apply principles of persuasion when developing written arguments.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of argumentation and the path-to-argumentation approach through analysis of reading texts within the scope of the course.
Identification and evaluation of claims, supporting evidence, and assumptions in written texts.
Principles of persuasion and the rhetorical triangle (ethos, pathos, logos).
Key components of effective argumentation: thesis statement, supporting evidence, engagement with counterarguments and refutation, integrative conclusion.
Structure and organization of argumentative essays.
Practice in argumentative writing through structured writing topics.
Two in-class argumentative writing tasks involving a draft-feedback-revision cycle.
Integration of reading comprehension and vocabulary development with writing tasks.
Preparation for midterm exam, writing exam, and final exam.
